symptom_label: Itchy or tingling mouth, lips, tongue or throat
match_keywords: itchy mouth; itchy throat; tingling lips; scratchy throat; itchy tongue; tingling tongue
plain_explanation: This can happen within minutes of eating certain raw fruits, vegetables or nuts. It is sometimes called oral allergy syndrome or pollen-food allergy syndrome.
what_it_may_suggest: Sometimes linked to pollen-related proteins such as PR-10 proteins or profilins, but other causes are possible.
safety_note: If swelling spreads, or there is throat tightness or breathing difficulty, seek urgent medical help.

symptom_label: Swelling of lips, tongue or throat
match_keywords: swollen lips; swollen tongue; throat swelling; puffy mouth; swollen mouth
plain_explanation: Swelling around the mouth can occur with allergic reactions. Swelling of the throat is more concerning because it can affect breathing.
what_it_may_suggest: Can occur in allergic reactions; severity depends on the person and exposure.
safety_note: Throat swelling, voice change, or breathing difficulty is an emergency.

match_keywords: hives; rash; itchy skin; welts; urticaria; itchy skin rash
plain_explanation: Hives are raised, itchy patches on the skin. They can occur in allergic reactions but also have many non-allergic causes.
what_it_may_suggest: May occur with food allergy, but a rash alone does not prove an allergy.
safety_note: Hives with vomiting, dizziness, or breathing difficulty needs emergency care.

symptom_label: Sneezing, runny nose or itchy eyes
match_keywords: sneezing; runny nose; itchy eyes; hay fever; rhinitis; blocked nose
plain_explanation: These are common symptoms of allergic rhinitis, often called hay fever. They may occur with pollen allergy.
what_it_may_suggest: Often related to pollen allergens; some people also react to certain plant foods.
safety_note: Wheezing or shortness of breath needs medical attention.

symptom_label: Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea
match_keywords: stomach pain; vomiting; diarrhoea; nausea; cramps; stomach upset
plain_explanation: Digestive symptoms can occur in food allergy, but they are also caused by many non-allergic conditions, including infections and food intolerance.
what_it_may_suggest: More stable food allergens may be more likely to cause gut symptoms than easily digested pollen-related proteins.
safety_note: Vomiting with hives, dizziness, or breathing trouble needs emergency care.

symptom_label: Trouble breathing, wheezing, dizziness or fainting
match_keywords: wheeze; difficulty breathing; shortness of breath; faint; dizzy; throat tight; collapse; anaphylaxis
plain_explanation: These can be signs of a severe allergic reaction. They need urgent medical assessment.
what_it_may_suggest: May indicate anaphylaxis, a serious whole-body allergic reaction.
safety_note: EMERGENCY: seek immediate medical help or use an adrenaline auto-injector if prescribed. This website cannot assess an emergency.

symptom_label: Reacts to raw fruit but tolerates cooked fruit
match_keywords: raw apple only; cooked is fine; apple pie ok; juice ok; raw fruit but not cooked
plain_explanation: Some plant-food proteins, especially PR-10 proteins, are changed by heating. This can make cooked fruit easier to tolerate for some people.
what_it_may_suggest: May fit a pollen-related pattern, but it is not a reliable safety test.
safety_note: Never use cooking as a way to test whether a food is safe. Ask an allergist.
